items.question: The demand function for a good is Q = 120 − 4P, where Q is quantity in units and P is price in ₹ per unit. What is the point price elasticity of demand (in absolute value) at P = ₹20?
items.explanation: Point elasticity = (dQ/dP) × (P/Q). Slope dQ/dP = −4. At P = 20, Q = 120 − 80 = 40. So |e| = 4 × 20/40 = 2. Demand is elastic at this point.

why_not.C: Used Q/P inverted ratio logic: took P/Q only and ignored the slope of 4.
why_not.B: Took the slope alone as elasticity, forgetting to multiply by P/Q.
why_not.D: Divided P/Q by the slope instead of multiplying: 0.5 ÷ 4 is wrong, giving 0.125-type error.

items.exam_tip: Point elasticity = slope × P/Q. Slope of the demand line alone is never elasticity.
items.reviewer_note: Option D why_not wording: 0.25 may arise from (P/Q)/slope ×... check; minor.
check_notes: Switched to a new topic because the first one couldn't be verified
Writer: Option D why_not wording: 0.25 may arise from (P/Q)/slope ×... check; minor.

items.question: Hari sent 1,000 units to Mohan on consignment at cost ₹300 per unit. Hari paid freight ₹30,000 and transit insurance ₹10,000. Mohan paid octroi at arrival ₹20,000 and godown rent ₹15,000. 800 units were sold. Value of unsold stock?
items.explanation: Non-recurring expenses up to the godown (freight, insurance, octroi) are added for all 1,000 units, whoever paid. Godown rent is recurring and excluded. Cost per unit is ₹360, so 200 units are ₹72,000.

why_not.B: Ignores octroi paid by the consignee; only consignor's expenses were added.
why_not.C: Adds godown rent, which is a recurring expense and never forms part of stock.
why_not.A: Takes 200 units at ₹300 cost only, leaving out non-recurring expenses.

items.exam_tip: Add non-recurring expenses up to the godown, whoever paid; never add godown rent or selling costs.
items.calculation:
cost = 1000 * 300
nonrec = 30000 + 10000 + 20000
total = cost + nonrec
answer = total / 1000 * 200
check_notes: Checker: The question doesn't say that stock is valued under AS 2 (or the usual consignment convention). It also doesn't say whether godown rent is a selling or storage expense. A student who included the rent would get C (₹75,000). The correct treatment is standard, but the wording could state it.
Checker: The question doesn't say if the stock is valued at cost or at net realisable value. It also doesn't say that the 800 units sold were sold at a price at or above cost.

items.topic: Sale of Goods Act: Condition and Warranty
items.question: Asha bought a specific used car from Bala, described in the contract as "2022 model". She took delivery, used it for four months, then found it was a 2021 model. The contract has no term on this point. What is Asha's legal position?
options: She may only treat the breach as a breach of warranty and claim damages
The contract is void because of mutual mistake about the model year
She may reject the car and recover the full price paid
She has no remedy because of the rule of caveat emptor
items.explanation: Description of goods is a condition. But once the buyer has accepted the goods in a non-severable contract, the breach of condition can only be treated as a breach of warranty, unless the contract says otherwise. So only damages are available.

why_not.C: Right to repudiate is lost once the buyer accepts the goods; she overlooks acceptance by use.
why_not.B: Wrong description by seller is not a mutual mistake; the contract stays valid.
why_not.D: Caveat emptor does not protect a seller who sells goods that do not match the description.

items.exam_tip: Condition breached + goods accepted (non-severable contract) = treat as warranty breach: damages only, no rejection.
items.applicability: Sale of Goods Act, 1930 – condition vs warranty
items.reviewer_note: Based on Sale of Goods Act s.13(2) (breach of condition treated as breach of warranty after acceptance); no section number used in text.
check_notes: Writer: Based on Sale of Goods Act s.13(2) (breach of condition treated as breach of warranty after acceptance); no section number used in text.

Checker: "The contract has no term on this point" is unclear. It could be read as no express term on the model year, which seems to clash with the "2022 model" description. It is probably meant to say the contract does not exclude the s.13(2) rule, and it should say that directly.

Checker: The question doesn't say whether Asha could reasonably have checked the model year at delivery (for example from the registration papers). That would help settle that she accepted the car, though four months of use and passing of ownership already support the key.

items.question: Process X: 10,000 units input; material ₹4,01,000, conversion ₹2,12,500. Normal loss 1,000 units (scrap ₹5/unit). Output 7,500 units; closing WIP 1,000 (materials 100%, conversion 50%); abnormal loss 500 units (fully worked). Net cost of abnormal loss, after its scrap value, is:
items.explanation: Normal loss scrap reduces material cost. Equivalent units: materials 9,000; conversion 8,500. Abnormal loss is valued at full cost per unit (₹69), then its scrap value of ₹5 per unit is deducted.

why_not.B: Forgot to deduct the scrap value of abnormal loss units.
why_not.D: Treated abnormal loss as only 50% complete for conversion cost.
why_not.A: Counted only material cost of abnormal loss and ignored conversion cost.

items.exam_tip: Normal loss scrap lowers the pool; abnormal loss is costed like good units, then credited with its own scrap value.
items.reviewer_note: Assumes abnormal loss is 100% complete for materials and conversion, stated in the question.
check_notes: Writer: Assumes abnormal loss is 100% complete for materials and conversion, stated in the question.
Checker: The question doesn't say that normal-loss scrap is credited against material cost. This is the standard treatment, and the alternative treatments are unlikely to be used.
Checker: Option B (₹34,500) is the gross cost of abnormal loss, which is a plausible distractor. The wording "after its scrap value" makes it clear that B is not the answer.

items.question: Under Ind AS 36, a CGU has goodwill ₹20 lakh, plant ₹60 lakh and building ₹40 lakh. Its recoverable amount is ₹90 lakh. Plant's fair value less costs of disposal is ₹57 lakh (value in use not determinable). Carrying amount of building after impairment?
items.explanation: Loss ₹30 lakh. Goodwill absorbs ₹20 lakh. Balance ₹10 lakh goes pro rata: plant ₹6 lakh, building ₹4 lakh. Plant cannot fall below ₹57 lakh, so only ₹3 lakh; excess ₹3 lakh goes to building. Building loss ₹7 lakh.

why_not.C: Ignored the floor on plant; did not reallocate the excess loss to building.
why_not.A: Spread whole loss pro rata including goodwill instead of writing off goodwill first.
why_not.D: Reduced building by only the reallocated ₹3 lakh and forgot its own pro rata share.

items.exam_tip: Ind AS 36 order: goodwill first, then pro rata; no asset below its FVLCD, VIU or zero; reallocate the excess.
items.calculation:
total = 6000000+4000000+2000000
loss = total - 9000000
rem = loss - 2000000
bshare = rem*4000000/(6000000+4000000)
plantmax = 6000000 - 5700000
plantshare = rem*6000000/10000000
excess = plantshare - plantmax
answer = 4000000 - bshare - excess
items.reviewer_note: Reallocation of excess loss is pro rata to other assets; only building remains, so it takes all of it.
check_notes: Writer: Reallocation of excess loss is pro rata to other assets; only building remains, so it takes all of it.

items.topic: Ind AS 33 - EPS with Rights Issue
items.question: FY 2026-27: 10,00,000 equity shares at 1 April 2026. On 1 October 2026 a 1-for-4 rights issue at ₹60 was made; fair value just before exercise was ₹110. Profit for equity holders ₹1,41,00,000. Basic EPS under Ind AS 33 is:
items.explanation: Rights issue has a bonus element. TERP = ₹100, so the factor is 110/100 = 1.10. Pre-issue shares are weighted at 1.10 for 6 months; all shares for 6 months. Weighted shares 11,75,000; EPS = ₹12.00.

why_not.A: Ignored the bonus element; simple time-weighting of 11,25,000 shares.
why_not.D: Used all 12,50,000 shares for the full year, ignoring the issue date.
why_not.C: Applied the bonus factor to the rights shares as well as the old shares.

items.exam_tip: Rights issue: TERP first, factor = FV before ÷ TERP, apply only to shares outstanding before the issue.
